Yes — the page appears to load correctly. There are **5 chessboards**, all rendered with visible pieces (no blank boards and no visible error messages/overlays). One board has colored arrows + letter labels drawn on it; the others are clean.

- Bottom‑right region: empty white space (no sixth board).

- Each labeled panel contains a complete 8×8 grid with a proper light/dark checker pattern.
- Piece glyphs (rook, knight, bishop, queen, king, pawn in both white and black fills) are clearly rendered on every board; the FEN board shows an irregular but valid-looking arrangement, confirming FEN loading works.
- The "fixed arrows" board shows distinct colored line strokes with arrowheads and round A–F badges, confirming the arrow/label feature renders.
- No red error boxes, no stack traces, no "board failed to load" placeholders, and no empty/blank grids.

3) Caveats / uncertainty
- The on‑square coordinate labels are very small/low‑contrast, so I can't read every file/rank character with certainty (e.g., the mirrored board's exact leftmost file label).
- I'm judging "loads correctly" from the rendered screenshot only; I cannot see the browser console or network panel, so I can't rule out non‑visual JS warnings.
- The bottom‑right area is blank; that's just unused layout space, not an error, but flagging it in case a sixth board was expected.
